prompt: A long line of small round floating buoys strung along one thin rope, crossing the open sea in a gentle rising diagonal from the left towards the upper right, seen from slightly above. Partway along, a second thin rope with a few buoys of its own splits away from the main line, runs beside it for a stretch and then joins it again further on. The last buoy at the right end is slightly larger and carries a little bright cobalt blue #3D6FD9 pennant flag on a thin mast, the flag marked with a tiny off-white check mark. Every buoy sits half-submerged in the water with small ripples around it, the rope dipping lightly under the wave lines between buoys, all drawn in crisp off-white and ink grey line art with fine engraved shading, in the same engraved line as the sea. Richly detailed engraved nautical chart style, like a fine antique sea chart printed in two inks: the sea built from many layers of fine wave lines and hatching, line density highest in the deep water at the top and thinning steadily downwards, tonal bands from deep cerulean at the top to lighter cerulean at the bottom, bathymetric contour lines with small depth soundings drawn as tiny dots in the upper water, a delicate compass rose with fine tick marks in the top left corner, subtle foam strokes and a few glints of light on the crests. The lower third is calm open water in a lighter cerulean tint, with only sparse, thin, pale wave lines and nothing floating in it. Crisp sharp lines of several weights, intricate but calm, premium print quality, high detail, elegant. No realistic objects, no photographic rendering, no glow, no text, no letters, no numbers, no watermark, no horizon, no sky, no clouds, full-bleed edge to edge, the sea covering the whole image, no border, no frame, the line of buoys small, kept within the upper two thirds and weighted towards the right. Palette strictly limited to medium cerulean ocean blue #0072a8 and its tints and shades, off-white #fbfcfd, ink grey #13212b and a touch of bright cobalt blue #3D6FD9 on the pennant only.
